input.question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?
input.ground_truth: Certainly if one considers the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid empire as the "end of antiquity" and the beginning of the early medieval era. It is the last great war because the next one defined the end of the era. Then the question becomes is the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid Empire the best delimiting event between late antiquity and early medieval. There's a lot of good points stating that it is, since the fall of the Sassanid empire meant the Byzantine Empire was then the only surviving great power from classical antiquity. All of the other powers of the era are relatively new. The Muslim conquest of North Africa and Levant also split off those regions from what the classical Roman world. A parallel can be drawn to how the fall of the Soviet Union marked the end of the cold war.

Question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?

Okay! Let’s break this down like you’re five.

Imagine you have a big box of old toys. These toys are from a long, long time ago—they’re “ancient” toys. Now, some people play with these old toys and call them “antiquity” toys.

Now, there was a big fight (that’s the war) between two leaders: Heraclius and Khusro II. This fight happened a long, long time ago, but not as long ago as when the pyramids were built.

James Howard-Johnston said this fight was “the last great war of antiquity.” That means he thinks it was the last really big, important fight that belonged to the world of those old “antiquity” toys.

But some people might say: “Wait! After this fight, the world started to change a lot. The new kinds of toys (or ways of living) came in, and things weren’t the same as before.” So maybe this fight was the very last one that was still like the old times.

So, James Howard-Johnston thought this war was special because it was the last big one before everything changed. But other people might not agree—they might say the world changed a little before, or after, or maybe not right away.

In simple words:  
James Howard-Johnston called this war “the last great war of the old times” because he thought it was the last really big, important fight before everything became new and different. But some people might think the world already started changing before or after this war.
